newsitem.title: GERMANY: MG seeks managerial control of AGIV.
newsitem.headline: MG seeks managerial control of AGIV.

text.p: Metallgesellschaft AG said on Monday it intended to take managerial control of industrial holding company AGIV.
MG said earlier it planned to buy 49.99 percent of AGIV from BHF-Bank and that the deal was still subject to approval by the supervisory board and cartel authorities.
MG does not own any AGIV shares yet. An MG spokesman contacted by Reuters declined to comment on whether MG planned to buy additional shares in AGIV on top of the 49.99 percent stake.

Given the fact that less than 100 percent of a company's capital usually attends annual general meetings in Germany, a stake of 49.99 percent would in theory be sufficient to secure a majority of shareholder votes.
Energieversorgung Schwaben AG, a regional utility, holds more than 10 percent of AGIV. About 40 percent of the shares are widely distributed.
AGIV shares leaped three marks ($1.89) to 28.30 on the news in pre-bourse electronic trade.
